definition: Segmenting audio by who spoke when ("speaker 1: ..., speaker 2: ..."), typically via speaker embeddings plus clustering, or end-to-end neural diarization.
details: Segmenting audio by who spoke when ("speaker 1: ..., speaker 2: ..."), typically via speaker embeddings plus clustering, or end-to-end neural diarization. Essential for meetings, call centers, and any multi-speaker transcript.

explainer.lead: Speaker diarization segments audio by who spoke when, producing transcripts labelled like "speaker 1: ..." and "speaker 2: ...". It matters for meetings, call centers, and any multi-speaker transcript where knowing the speaker is essential.

tiers.eli5: It is the process that listens to a recording and marks each stretch as coming from speaker 1, speaker 2, and so on, like labelling the dialogue in a script.
tiers.practitioner: Common approaches combine speaker embeddings with clustering, or use end-to-end neural diarization. A pitfall is that diarization labels who spoke when but does not attach real identities to those labels.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as segmenting audio by who spoke when, typically via speaker embeddings plus clustering, or end-to-end neural diarization. No formula or quantitative limits are given.

explainer.example: A recorded meeting is processed so the transcript reads "speaker 1: ..." for one participant and "speaker 2: ..." for another, without naming either person.
